Niubash <version> — a bash-compatible shell that feels at home on Windows.

Usage:  niu [GNU long option] [option] ...
        niu [GNU long option] [option] script-file ...
        niu -c <cmd>         Run a command then exit
        niu -C <cmd>         Run one REPL-style command then exit
        niu setup           Re-run prompt/plugin setup
        niu font            Nerd Font detection & install recommendations
        niu doctor          Health-check the installation
        niu <script> [args]  Run a script file

GNU long options:
    --debug
    --debugger
    --dump-po-strings
    --dump-strings
    --help
    --init-file <file>
    --login
    --noediting
    --noprofile
    --norc
    --posix
    --pretty-print
    --rcfile <file>
    --restricted
    --verbose
    --version

Shell options:
    -ilrsD or -c command or -O shopt_option		(invocation only)
    -abefhkmnptuvxBCEHPT or -o option

    -c <command> runs the command string (the word after it becomes $0);
    -s reads commands from standard input; --init-file and --rcfile each
    take <file>, replacing the default startup file (profile chain / rc).

Script debugging:
  niu --debug <script> [args]  Debug a script in the interactive CLI
                               (commands come from the controlling terminal)
  niu --dap <script> [args]    Serve the Debug Adapter Protocol on stdio
  niu --debug --dap <script>   The spelled-out editor launch form
  niu --debugger <script>      Source the GNU bashdb starter (GNU parity)
  --dap with no script runs a pure DAP server; the client's `launch`
  request names the program. `--debug` with -c, -s, or -i keeps the
  legacy extdebug-arming behavior (no debugger frontend).

Type `niu -c "help set"` for more information about shell options.
Type `niu -c help` for more information about shell builtin commands.
Report bugs at <https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/issues>.
Niubash home page: <https://github.com/unixwin/niubash>.

Options:
  -h, --help                Show this help
  -V, --version             Version and component info
  -c <command>              Execute a command ad-hoc
  -C, --repl-command <cmd>  Execute one non-interactive REPL command
  Verbatim handoff (execute a base64-encoded command, no quoting):
      --encoded-command <b64>  canonical spelling
      -EncodedCommand <b64>    PowerShell spelling, matched case-insensitively
      --ec <b64>               short alias for --encoded-command
                               optional `v1:` prefix guards against MSYS path rewrite
      --cwd-state <file>       Restore the recorded directory at startup and
                               record the final directory back on exit

Bash-compatible invocation options (GNU semantics, parsed by the engine):
  -c <command>              Execute the next non-option argument as a command
  -i                        Force the interactive shell
  -l, --login               Act as a login shell
  -r, --restricted          Restricted shell (restricts cd and PATH/ENV changes)
  -s                        Read commands from standard input
  -D                        Dump locale-translatable strings and exit
  -o <option>               Set a `set -o` option by name
  -O <shopt>                Set a `shopt` option by name
  -a                        allexport: export all new and modified variables
  -b                        notify: report the status of terminated background jobs
  -e                        errexit: exit immediately if a command fails
  -f                        noglob: disable pathname expansion
  -h                        hashall: remember the location of executed commands
  -k                        keyword: keep keyword=value arguments in the environment
  -m                        monitor: enable job control
  -n                        noexec: read commands without executing them
  -p                        privileged: do not reset the effective uid
  -t                        onecmd: exit after reading and executing one command
  -u                        nounset: error when expanding an unset variable
  -v, --verbose             verbose: echo input lines as they are read
  -x                        xtrace: trace expanded commands
  -B                        braceexpand: enable brace expansion
  -C                        noclobber: refuse to overwrite existing files with >
  -E                        errtrace: inherit the ERR trap in functions and subshells
  -H                        histexpand: enable ! history expansion
  -P                        physical: do not resolve symlinks in cd
  -T                        functrace: inherit DEBUG and RETURN traps
  Invoke the binary as `bash` or `sh` (shim or symlink) for the full
  byte-for-byte GNU usage form: `bash --help`.

  --install-wt-profile      Add/update the Windows Terminal profile
      --set-default         Also set Niubash as the WT default profile
      --quiet               Suppress non-error profile output
  --install-wt-shortcuts    Rewrite desktop/Start-menu shortcuts (WT form
                            `wt.exe -p Niubash` when WT is detected)
      --update-only         Only touch shortcut files that already exist
      --quiet               Suppress non-error shortcut output
  --self-update             Download and run the latest release installer
      --check               Only report the latest release
      --dry-run             Download installer without running it
  self-update               REPL command: update Niubash and exit this shell
  update-niubash            Alias for self-update

  plugin add <id|owner/repo|url|path>
                            Install an external plugin source (untrusted)
  plugin list [--json]      Sources, their assets, activation state
  plugin enable|disable <t> Activate or deactivate a source or asset
  plugin update|sync|restore|rollback|clean
                            Lockfile verbs (vim-plug/lazy.nvim-style)
  plugin trust <id>         Review and activate a source's assets
  plugin migrate-rc [--diff]
                            Read-only migration report for legacy managed
                            blocks (never writes the rc)
  plugin discover [--verbose]
                            Read-only overview of external plugin sources
  plugin source <command>   Full source protocol (add/trust/sign/verify/
                            remove/update/rollback/list)
  plugin recipe <command>   Recipe index (list/show/add)
  plugin distro <command>   Collections (list/import/remove/apply)
  plugin mirror <command>   Git fetch mirroring (list/show/set)
  plugin ui                 Menu UI (sections by state, same verbs)

  skill install|status      Install/check the AI agent skill bundle
                            ([--target claude|zcode|cursor|all|<dir>])

  --completion-probe <line> [cursor]  Debug: print completion candidates

Configuration: ~/.niubashrc for interactive startup (primary-only; no automatic legacy migration)

Environment:
  NIU_ENV=<file>          Non-interactive init file sourced by -c, scripts, and stdin
                          before running the command (bash BASH_ENV is also honored,
                          NIU_ENV takes precedence). Unset by default, keeping -c fast.
  BASH_ENV=<file>         GNU bash compatible: same as NIU_ENV, lower precedence.
  NIU_LANG=<lang>         Setup wizard language (zh / en). Falls back to the
                          Windows UI language, then LC_ALL/LANG.

Home: <https://unixwin.dev>
Docs & downloads: <https://unixwin.dev>
